clue.text: General view of community work in one back number

parts.note: the community at large is the public
OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for number is turned round to read the other way

explanation.surface: A survey of what a community thinks, filed in a back issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO into ON at the end of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The general view of a population is the consensus judgement held by most people.

clue.text: Advance account of state journey?

parts.note: a royal tour of the realm was once called a progress, so a write-up of one is literally a report of a progress, punning on an update on how far work has advanced

explanation.surface: A preview of a royal tour of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An update on how far work has advanced, read as a write-up of a sovereign's ceremonial tour.

clue.text: Restrained rage over note

parts.note: a bate is an old British word for a fit of temper or rage
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone holding back their anger over a message.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Held back, as in waiting with breath held in suspense.

clue.text: His behaviour spoils the public image

definitions.text: His behaviour spoils the public image

parts.words: His behaviour spoils the public image
parts.note: read literally, this is someone who smashes religious images; figuratively, someone who attacks cherished beliefs and reputations

explanation.surface: A person whose conduct ruins a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker of sacred images, and by extension one who attacks established beliefs.

clue.text: Method of booking popular carriage …

definitions.meaning: a volume collecting several works or episodes in one is a way of putting things in a book
a horse-drawn public vehicle for everyone, from Latin 'for all'

explanation.surface: How to reserve a seat on a favourite coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected edition of several works, and the old word for a public bus open to all.

clue.text: … alternatively, seasonable dates changed

parts.note: fruit in season is 'in', so in fashion or in season gives IN

indicators.note: changed says the letters of dates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Or else, dates suited to the season were moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges DATES into STEAD, placed after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as a substitute or as the other option.

clue.text: Some depressing ecclesiastic providing St Paul's chapter-heading

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gloomy churchman heading the cathedral chapter of St Paul's.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'providing', which is only a link word. Dean W. R. Inge of St Paul's was nicknamed 'the Gloomy Dean', so 'depressing ecclesiastic' also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The dean heads a cathedral chapter, and William Inge was Dean of St Paul's in London.

clue.text: Their figures are barely perceptible

parts.note: barely here means unclothed, not scarcely, so these are people whose bodies are seen bare

explanation.surface: People whose shapes can hardly be made out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists go about without clothes, so their bodies are visible in the bare.

clue.text: Leader of movement, normal type, who, gets paid by cheque

parts.note: the standard model is the normal type
a cheque payable to bearer pays out to whoever holds it

explanation.surface: A movement's head is an ordinary sort, paid by cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The person carrying the flag at the front of a cause leads it.

clue.text: They tend to exhaust one's income

definitions.text: They tend to exhaust one's income

parts.words: They tend to exhaust one's income
parts.note: spending, the money going out, uses up what comes in, with exhaust also hinting at an outlet

explanation.surface: Things that drain one's earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Expenditure is money spent, which eats up earnings.

clue.text: Attained by bribery ?

parts.note: attained can mean reached, and a phrase for reached also means corrupted by a bribe

explanation.surface: Something won through a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Reached, and also the idiom for corrupted or nobbled with a bribe.

clue.text: Receiver of internal aid perhaps or outside backing

indicators.note: internal says the next letters go inside another piece
outside says the reversed word sits around the other piece
backing says the word or is read in reverse
perhaps says the letters of aid may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipient of help from inside, or support from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes ADI from AID; 'backing' makes RO from OR, which goes 'outside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set is an apparatus that receives broadcast signals.

clue.text: Drumming heard from this sugar plant

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken and a different spelling entered

parts.note: drumming is a beat

explanation.surface: A drumming noise coming from a sugar plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is the crop grown to make sugar.

clue.text: Is Jenny the feminine of Jack?

definitions.text: Is Jenny the feminine of Jack?

parts.words: Is Jenny the feminine of Jack?
parts.note: Jenny is the traditional name for a small brown bird, and a female naval rating is the counterpart of Jack Tar the sailor

explanation.surface: A question about whether Jenny is the female form of Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Tar is slang for a British sailor; in Britain the women's naval service members were known by a bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small bird called Jenny and a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service.

clue.text: Sweetener changes outcome in car-chase

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the following words are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sweetener alters how a car chase ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes outcome' rearranges the ten letters of IN CARCHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial sugar substitute used to sweeten food and drink.

clue.text: Bulbous seaside types are southern writers

parts.note: quill pens are old writing implements

explanation.surface: Fat seaside characters turn out to be authors from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea squills are bulb plants growing on coasts.

clue.text: Detaches loose bearing with new style terminal

indicators.note: terminal says the last piece goes at the end

parts.note: unfast is an old word for not fixed, loose
E, east, is a compass bearing
NS is the abbreviation for New Style, the Gregorian calendar

explanation.surface: Something comes away, loose and fitted with a newly styled end.
explanation.walkthrough: New Style (NS) is the calendar Britain adopted in 1752.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoes or releases fastenings, setting things free.

clue.text: Notices in the river a salt lake

indicators.note: in says the notices go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
ads are notices

explanation.surface: Notices posted in the river beside a salt lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked salt lake between Israel and Jordan.

clue.text: Did not agree to having another safety device

explanation.surface: Someone rejected having another safety device fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Declined, and also re-equipped with a new electrical fuse.

clue.text: Was love of the 'theatre in the thirties so sad?

definitions.text: Was love of the 'theatre in the thirties so sad?

parts.words: Was love of the 'theatre in the thirties so sad?
parts.note: in the 1930s Depression the unemployment benefit queue was crowded, so the dole was full, like a packed theatre

explanation.surface: A question whether theatre-going in the 1930s was gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit, which many drew in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful, sorrowful, read as the dole being full.

clue.text: RAF type, roughly treated, put on a charge

parts.note: AC is an aircraftman in the Royal Air Force
C, circa, means roughly
used means treated

explanation.surface: An airman, roughly handled, is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged with an offence, as a defendant is.

clue.text: Eager to change into a T-shirt

indicators.note: change says the letters of the following words are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Keen to get changed into a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'a T-shirt'; the held text lost the T. 'change into' rearranges ATSHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsting for something, figuratively keen or longing.

clue.text: Smart two-way way to travel, some say

definitions.text: two-way way to travel, some say
definitions.meaning: the folk origin is Port Out, Starboard Home, the shady cabins on voyages to India

explanation.surface: A stylish return journey, according to some.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket and classy, with a popular though false origin in ocean-liner cabin booking.

clue.text: River with beginning but no end

indicators.note: but no end says the last letter is removed

parts.note: alpha is the first letter, the beginning

explanation.surface: A river with a source but no mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred river of Xanadu in Coleridge's poem.

clue.text: Rotten way to make pa blanch

definitions.meaning: spoilt, as a bad egg is
to confuse or befuddle someone is a way to make dad go pale

explanation.surface: A nasty way to make father turn pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding the letters to PA would also make PADDLE, a further joke on 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled eggs are rotten; as a verb it means to muddle someone.

clue.text: Film star to act King Cole

parts.note: do means act
Nat King Cole was an American singer

explanation.surface: A film star plays Nat King Cole.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Donat was a British film star of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Donat starred in The 39 Steps and won an Oscar.

clue.text: Can this mountain be the end of a humiliating trip?

definitions.text: Can this mountain be the end of a humiliating trip?

parts.words: Can this mountain be the end of a humiliating trip?
parts.note: a Greek peak whose name sounds like falling on one's backside, the end of a humiliating stumble

explanation.surface: Whether climbing a mountain could end in an embarrassing tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain in Thessaly, Greece, famously piled with Pelion.

clue.text: How one pulls in the right fishes

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
eels are fishes

explanation.surface: An angler drawing in the right fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler winds the line on a spool to draw the catch in.

clue.text: No native warning, driving by the stormy Niger

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout when driving

indicators.note: stormy says the letters of Niger are tossed about

explanation.surface: No local, a golfer shouts a warning while driving by the turbulent Niger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' points to golf, where FORE is shouted; 'stormy' rearranges NIGER into IGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from another country is not a native.

clue.text: Hawthorne's a red

parts.note: in Nathaniel Hawthorne's novel the heroine must wear a crimson letter A, so a red A

explanation.surface: Hawthorne is a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Nathaniel Hawthorne's novel about an adulteress branded with a red A.
